traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 324 Scrophulariaceae (its core: Verbascum, Scrophularia, Nemesia, Sutera), 227 Buddleiaceae, 339 Myoporaceae and 340 Selaginaceae, which APG joins as Scrophulariaceae (Hutchinson's figwort family also held what APG puts in Plantaginaceae and Orobanchaceae): herbs or shrubs, rarely small trees; leaves alternate, opposite or whorled; no stipules; flowers mostly irregular, the butterfly bushes' regular; corolla united, a tube of 4 or 5 lobes, often two-lipped; stamens 4 (two long, two short) or 2, rarely 5; ovary superior, of two cells; fruit a capsule, the myoporums' a drupe. The order (Lamiales) states the stipules, the ovary and the two carpels.
